venture.description: A portable, connected cable resistance training machine with an accompanying coaching app.
venture.note: The ask is for $500,000 for 2.5% equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder introduces himself, explains the problem of inactivity, and demonstrates his portable, connected cable resistance training machine.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks to verify if the machine can really adjust the weight from 3 pounds to 300 pounds.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder invites Robert to come up and try the machine to see the resistance for himself.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert agrees and walks up to try the machine.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks to confirm if she heard the 300 pounds claim correctly.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms that the claim is absolutely correct.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains the cables and the material they are made of to Robert.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks what weight setting is currently on the machine.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder tells him it is set to level 5.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond jokingly compliments Robert's effort.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder helps Robert adjust the dial to a higher resistance level and tells him the equivalent weight.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert expresses amazement that so much resistance comes from such a small machine.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder agrees with Robert's observation.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin questions the valuation and asks when the company started and what the year-over-year sales figures are.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains that product development took over five years, but they first started shipping in July of last year.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks how much revenue they generated in sales last year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states they did four million dollars in sales last year.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori expresses surprise and being impressed by the sales figure.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks what the sales figures are for the current year so far.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states they have done over eight million dollars in sales so far this year.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert acknowledges the impressive sales growth.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori expresses dislike for over-the-door resistance bands and asks how the machine accommodates other exercises.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains the versatility of the machine, noting it can be used on a door, wall track, tree, or fence.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks how he came up with the idea and what his professional background is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder shares his 25-year background as an automotive engineer and how traveling inspired him to create portable resistance.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond asks for the cost to make and sell the product, wanting to get straight to the numbers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder begins by stating that the retail value is 849 dollars.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks to confirm the retail price of 849 dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms the price is 849 dollars.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond asks if the sample boxes in front of them are theirs to keep.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms they can keep the samples.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder details the costs, stating a landed cost of 205 dollars and an additional 20 dollars for shipping.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks if all their sales are direct to consumer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms that 97% of their sales are direct to consumer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks how they are acquiring so many customers, wondering if it's due to Covid-19 trends.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder agrees with the Covid factor and adds that they spend heavily on marketing.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks what their monthly cash burn rate is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states their essential burn is about 100,000 dollars per month.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks if slowing down their marketing spend would make the company profitable.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder responds that they make money on every unit sold.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks directly if the business is cash flow positive this year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder says the answer is yes and no, starting to explain that they reinvest the money.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin interrupts, asserting that cash flow is binary and it must be one or the other.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder insists they are positive but explains that they reinvest all the money back into the business.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond voices understanding, acknowledging that it is a competitive business that requires grinding it out.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder adds that they currently have over 3,000 daily users on their app.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks how much profit they actually made on the four million dollars in sales last year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states they made just over 50,000 dollars.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks if they expect to make or lose money on the projected eight million in sales this year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder deflects by revising the sales projection, stating they will likely reach over 12 million.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert repeats his question, asking if they will make or lose money on that amount.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder admits they will probably be close to breaking even.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert challenges him, pointing out that this means he is currently burning money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder agrees with Robert's assessment.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark defends the founder, stating that investing money is necessary to scale and grow a business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder agrees with Mark and adds that they took a revenue-based line of credit to fund growth.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks what percentage of every dollar brought in goes toward paying off that line of credit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains the rate increased from 20% to 28%, and they currently hold over 5 million dollars in inventory.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks to verify the 5 million dollars in inventory figure.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks why they hold so much inventory and whether they were required to order certain quantities.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder calls it a judgment call and explains they signed a major endorsement deal with Shaq after meeting him.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks about the specifics of the deal with Shaq, specifically if they gave him equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms Shaq earns equity over a four-year period.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks exactly how much equity Shaq earns.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder says Shaq gets 1.25% this year and it can go up to 5%.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark points out that the company is currently in a very tough financial spot.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder concedes they are in a tough spot but notes the upcoming holiday season.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark counters that they lack the advertising budget needed to capitalize on the season.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder agrees it is hard and states that he needs the sharks' money and expertise.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond offers the $500,000 for 4% equity, plus a $25 royalty per unit until he recoups his investment.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert comments to the panel that Daymond's offer is not bad.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks the founder what specifically he needs from a shark partner.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder says he needs help opening doors in retail, hotels, and the military.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond points out that the founder has not acknowledged or responded to his offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder apologizes, explaining that the rapid questions distracted him.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond asks what the founder thinks of his offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder says it is a good deal but expresses reluctance about the royalty component.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks what their product return rate is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states that the return rate is less than 5%.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond jokingly remarks that he had an even better question.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder emphasizes that a return rate under 5% in consumer goods is incredible.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark challenges the founder, stating that he is overselling and the investors still have questions.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond complains that he has been waiting a long time for an answer to his offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark questions the need to spend money developing an app when everyone already has one, pointing out the financial losses.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks how much money could be saved if they did not have the app.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder defends the app, explaining that it displays real-time workout data rather than just counting reps.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin exits, citing a philosophical disagreement over the direction of spending money on an app.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark jokes with Daymond about becoming more valuable and states he wants to make an offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark offers $500,000 for 3% equity, plus 5% in advisory shares vesting on the same schedule as Shaq's.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert exits, stating that Mark's offer is far more generous than what he was prepared to offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond expresses shock that the founder has not engaged with his offer and asks if he answered all questions.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder tells Daymond there are no more questions and he needs to decide.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori exits, noting that Mark's offer is very good and her own offer would have taken more equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder thanks Daymond but turns to ask Mark a final question.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond withdraws his offer because the founder ignored it to speak with Mark.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder expresses surprise at Daymond withdrawing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder asks Mark if he can help replace their line of credit or assist with the inventory.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark says he won't commit to it now but it is something he commonly does and is on the table.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin reminds the founder that Mark's is the only offer remaining.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder accepts Mark's offer enthusiastically and thanks Daymond.

exchanges.label: what he needs from a shark

decisions.note: Offers the money for 4% equity, plus a $25 royalty per unit until the investment is paid back.
Disagrees with spending money on the app when there are already many apps available.
